newsitem.title: USA: Williams Cos. quarter aided by gain from transaction.
newsitem.headline: Williams Cos. quarter aided by gain from transaction.

text.p: Williams Cos Inc. reported higher second-quarter earnings Friday, aided by a one-time gain of $44.5 million related to its interest in WilTel Communications, LLC.
The diversified energy company had second-quarter profits of $107.8 million, or 65 cents a share, up from $80.4 million, or 48 cents a share a year earlier.
Revenues rose to $1.02 billion from $837.5 million a year earlier.

The company's Williams Communications Group joined with Nortel Communications Systems in April to create WilTel Communications, LLC. Williams retained 70 percent ownership and Northern Telecom a 30 percent minority interest in WilTel.
Williams accounted for the reduction in its ownership of stake as a partial sale, resulting in the $44.5 million gain.
The company reported second-quarter operating profit of $5.3 million in its Merchant Services business, down from operating profit of $15.9 million in the year ago period.
Merchant Services, part of the the Williams Energy Group, provides energy commodity trading, risk management, retail sales and service and energy capital.

While its natural gas physical trading volumes were 5 percent higher than a year ago, operating profit in the segment declined primarily due to substantially lower margins on natural gas and liquid petroleum trading activities and the expense of its expanding its business growth platforms, the company said.
Williams Cos., based in Tulsa, Okla., also said its natural gas pipelines were performing ahead of last year's record pace.
Williams Cos. stock was down 37.5 cents at $44.43.75 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
